column1: # check/spec/dynamic — non-concrete operands and the carriers they make.
# Every row here turns on anyq (Integer -> Any). Its return is not a
# concrete leaf, so its result is a NON-CONCRETE operand, and that is the
# only thing that reaches the dynamic-carrier family in carrier.go: the
# "is any operand non-concrete" predicates, the disjunct carriers, and the
# counting of which overloads stay reachable when the operand's type is
# not yet known. A fully concrete row cannot get there by construction.
# `dynamic(X)` in the expected column is a dynamic carrier over leaf X;
# a bare X is a strict one.
# --- a non-concrete return is carried dynamically, not collapsed to Any ---
1 anyq
1 anyq anyq
# --- feeding it to an OVERLOADED word keeps both arms live: the operand
#     conforms to neither Integer nor String yet, so the result is the
#     disjunction of what the reachable arms return ---
1 anyq twoq
1 anyq twoq twoq
column3: the disjunct re-enters and stays disjunct

column1: # --- feeding it to a MONOMORPHIC word commits to that word's return,
#     but the carrier stays dynamic: the value is still not known ---
1 anyq predq
1 anyq strq
# --- arity still applies to a dynamic operand: one operand is not two ---
1 anyq addq
# --- a dynamic operand alongside a concrete one is enough to dispatch ---
1 anyq 2 addq
1 anyq 2 anyq addq
# --- a dynamic residual survives a following quote ---
1 anyq [ 1 2 addq ]
